source_refs.title: Lore
source_refs.relevance: Grounds Delvehold's living-dungeon ontology, iterative runic industry, Greathold dependence, and the rule that in-world observers disagree about causes.

source_refs.title: Humans
source_refs.relevance: Primary owner for fragmented human politics, foreign dwarven rail and pump dependence, Mossgate bellhouses, table-kin apprentices, outage compensation, and household failure costs.

source_refs.title: Dwarves
source_refs.relevance: Grounds durable-work prestige, rail and household dependence, apprenticeship, and an ancestry-open path to Greathold Mastership without granting Brunna a civic seal.

source_refs.title: Mastership and citizenship
source_refs.relevance: Grounds the limits of apprenticeship and civic authority, apprentice rights to food, instruction, tools, appeal, and refusal, and the distinction between household custom and civic sealing.

source_refs.title: Runic engineering
source_refs.relevance: Grounds spell-engine operation, the manual origin of reliable runes, null-first apprentice training, rail engines, and narrow model-specific technician displacement.

source_refs.title: Dwarven industry
source_refs.relevance: Grounds rune locomotives, public infrastructure, company and labor interests, local rationing institutions, and the shared crystal-contract dependency of rail, food, heat, and drainage.

source_refs.title: International crisis
source_refs.relevance: Grounds foreign fields and harvests using dwarven pumps and rail, tightening trade conflict, and the civilian reach of attempts to interrupt extraction systems.

source_refs.title: Industrial escalation
source_refs.relevance: Grounds the causal loop in which pumps enable seams, output pays for rail, defensive failures drive new orders, and honest reporting still assumes service must continue.

source_refs.title: The Greathold
source_refs.relevance: Grounds the foreign infrastructure's Greathold origin, distributed civic authority, rail corridors, apprenticeship practice, and centuries of mixed-species institutions along the mountain spine.

historical_context.time_period: During tightening foreign trade restrictions and infrastructure dependency, before direct military intervention becomes ordinary.
historical_context.location: East Bellhouse, attached to the rail platform and alley lift of Mossgate, a human orchard-market town using a dwarven-built rail spur and imported crystal pump schedule.
historical_context.summary: A silent return bell makes the foreign rail contract domestic. A dwarf apprentice lodged with a human household must allocate the same hands among repair duty, food, water, missing-person accounting, and pressure on an operator that has not admitted an outage.

public_facts.text: Human cities buy dwarven rail and pump systems, creating constituencies for open crystal trade while displacing local magical work.
Mossgate's rail spur carries orchard produce, and its imported crystal schedule also drives local irrigation pumps.
Bellhouse households respond when the return bell fails by collecting children, checking infrastructure-dependent neighbours, feeding stranded workers, and lodging repair crews.
Table-kin is a reciprocal household relationship for foreign apprentices and grants neither inheritance nor a Greathold civic seal.
Runic apprentices learn null termination before useful effects, while industrial employers may narrow training to one engine model.

ambient_pressures.text: The operator owes registered bellhouses compensation only after it records an outage, so calling a stopped line a service pause leaves the first-night costs in homes.
The households feeding and bedding stranded people are also feeding and bedding the repair crews needed to restore the line.
The scene cannot prove whether the south-cut failure comes from shortage, policy, sabotage, ordinary breakdown, or ecological response; in-world knowledge remains partial.

groups.label: Mossgate platform bellhouses
institutional_logic: Answer the silent return bell before absence becomes injury, while keeping participation owned by households rather than the station.
material_incentives: Keep children, elders, commuters, and repair crews fed, watered, accounted for, and locally housed during interruptions.
internal_shames: Taking hospitality while hiding available stores
Letting a neighbour's child remain uncollected
prestige_markers: A white ladle answered by other houses
taboo_triggers: The operator treating voluntary care as free contracted capacity
Affectionate language used to erase a household's cost
emotional_display_norms: Fear becomes soup, cord knots, water carrying, dry jokes, and repeated glances toward the rail door.
trust_defaults: Trusts named reciprocal acts and witnessed records more than distant assurances or blank company slates.

groups.label: Dwarven railway branch staff in Mossgate
institutional_logic: Keep the contracted rail and pump schedule operating with standardized engines, bounded crews, and attributable service records.
material_incentives: Restore the south-cut feed, preserve apprentice placements, limit compensable outage hours, and keep scarce company stores controlled.
internal_shames: An apprentice unable to service the assigned model
A company record overruled by household evidence
prestige_markers: Repairs completed before the next schedule
taboo_triggers: Service language exposed as cost avoidance
emotional_display_norms: Alarm is translated into schedules, keys, fault boundaries, and clipped work assignments.
trust_defaults: Trusts sealed notices, trained hands, cabinet marks, and engine readings; depends on household care while treating it as external to the machine.

groups.label: Mossgate platform families and dependent neighbours
institutional_logic: Organize daily life around reliable trains, pumps, school collection, market shifts, and the expectation that known people return.
material_incentives: Locate absent wage earners, preserve water and medicine access, move produce, and keep children supervised.
internal_virtues: Not making need perform for help
internal_shames: Using private carts while leaving shared costs behind
Letting uncertainty become somebody else's domestic labor
prestige_markers: A household whose members are accounted for
A shift covered without hiding the cost
taboo_triggers: Blank official records during visible interruption
Outsiders treating the platform ward as politically passive dependence
emotional_display_norms: Worry is often carried through bowls kept warm, cords left red, and precise complaints about timetables.
trust_defaults: Trusts bellhouse response, visible signal state, and last-confirmed-route knowledge.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The neighbourhood must act while the operator is still deciding whether the stoppage counts, so care begins before reimbursement authority does.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Offer food, water, child collection, naming, and open-door choices before procedural recognition arrives.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Foreign apprentices owe technical duty to the railway and reciprocal care to the households that lodge them; an outage intensifies both claims at the same time.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Make Brunna choose where her body, skill, and time go without treating either work or kinship as unreal.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: Service classification decides whether household depletion appears as compensable infrastructure cost or disappears as private generosity.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Use the blank station slate, the household waiting board, sealed stores, and Hesta's notice as material record conflict.

observer_read: Community resilience outside the service contract
target_self_read: Households keeping named people alive and accounted for
Reciprocal care that creates claims of its own
misread_patterns: Treats voluntary response as spare capacity
Counts repair labor but not the labor making repair shifts possible
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Let Hesta understand the human cost while still carrying the notice that externalizes it; institutional dependence need not require personal stupidity.

observer_read: Employer claiming the same apprentice the household needs
target_self_read: Skilled crew protecting shared infrastructure under a bounded contract
misread_patterns: May treat every technical delay as cost avoidance
May underestimate the genuine limits of a starved feed and narrow crew
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Keep household anger precise while allowing the technical fault to remain real and difficult.

role_pressure_fields.summary: A foreign dwarf apprentice whose technical training, placement, household belonging, and care work make simultaneous claims on the same body.
obligations: Use null before touching a live feed
Do not pretend uncertainty is diagnosis
available_masks: Busy hands instead of open worry
failure_modes: Using kin language to hide exploitation
Claiming a distant fault from local evidence

role_pressure_fields.summary: A human household head who can open her own table but cannot classify the railway's failure or refill stores by moral force.
failure_modes: Treating an apprentice as either labor only or kin without work claims

role_pressure_fields.summary: A dwarven Master responsible for an exhausted repair crew, apprentice training, a dead feed, sealed company stores, and a service classification that protects the operator.
failure_modes: Accepting household support while refusing its terms
Sending narrow-trained workers into unfamiliar machinery
Letting schedule pressure outrun null safety

role_pressure_fields.summary: A child who understands rail dependence through bowls, cords, collection, and whether adults can say where her father is.
available_masks: Falling asleep beside the place kept open
failure_modes: Being used as a speech about stakes
Knowing company or technical facts no one has told her

known_context.text: Brunna knows East Bellhouse routine, its members and neighbours, the local station layout, her assigned engine model, null safety, and her own placement terms.

beliefs.text: Brunna believes useful work should survive inspection and that table-kin obligations are real even where the company does not record them.

misreads.text: Brunna may overestimate how far a correct local diagnosis or household record can move distant company authority.

must_not_know.text: Brunna must not know the south-cut failure's cause, Jory's exact position, or Hesta's final response before observable evidence reveals it.

known_context.text: Tamsin knows household stores, the bellhouse roster, platform routine, Jory's expected train, and what the operator compensates after a recorded outage.

beliefs.text: Tamsin believes a household may owe care without granting the railway free ownership of that capacity.

misreads.text: Tamsin may read genuine technical uncertainty as another contractual euphemism because the material cost reaches her before the explanation does.

must_not_know.text: Tamsin must not know whether the south-cut feed can be restored or where Jory's train stopped until the board or returning crew supplies evidence.

known_context.text: Hesta knows the fault is on the south-cut feed, which workers are available, what stores she can release, and the service classification on her notice.

beliefs.text: Hesta believes restoring the feed is the fastest way to reduce every dependent burden, while the service record remains a separate company obligation.

misreads.text: Hesta may count bellhouse beds and meals as ambient neighbourhood capacity instead of labor and inventory with claims on the railway.

must_not_know.text: Hesta must not know whether a proposed crew rotation will hold until households, fitters, and prepared stores visibly support it.

known_context.text: Nell knows who normally sits at the table, how waiting cords mark expected people, and that the silent bell means the household begins its watch.

beliefs.text: Nell treats Brunna as household kin because Brunna repeatedly shares work, worry, and return routines.

misreads.text: Nell may interpret a closed serving hatch as loss of belonging rather than depleted capacity.

must_not_know.text: Nell must not speak with adult knowledge of outage compensation, rail-feed engineering, or international crystal politics.

author_only_boundaries.text: Mossgate, its bellhouse watch, and table-kin custom are the authored lore elaboration. The exact branch outcome and named household incident remain fixture-local rather than canonical history.
The scene may show a starved south-cut feed but must not canonize sabotage, sanctions, ecological attack, or machine awakening as its cause.
Brunna's employer title Master describes Hesta's established professional authority; the fixture does not grant Brunna a Masterwork, independent workshop, or Greathold civic seal.

open_questions.question: Which Greathold workshop or consortium owns the Mossgate rail-and-pump service contract?
open_questions.notes: The fixture keeps the operator generic because ownership is not needed to dramatize household dependence and has not been supplied by the vault.

open_questions.question: How portable are model-specific railway apprenticeships between foreign branches and Greathold Mastership examinations?
open_questions.notes: The scene uses only Brunna's local placement and narrow engine training; a later Hearth or Ledger pass could ground credential portability.
